elements.element: Audit no more than once per 12 months
elements.evidence: "may not more than once in any twelve (12) month period"
"upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company"

elements.element: Performed by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality
elements.evidence: "through an independent third-party auditor bound by written confidentiality obligations"

elements.element: Vendor bears audit cost (shift only if underpayment exceeds 5%)
elements.evidence: "The fees incurred by HDI in connection with the inspection shall be borne by HDI." — unconditional vendor cost; the 5% shift-back condition is absent and its absence favours Customer

elements.element: No direct access to Customer systems
elements.evidence: "shall not include direct access to the Company's systems"
"not more than once in any twelve (12) month period"

elements.element: Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10%
elements.evidence: "fees incurred by HDI ... shall be borne by HDI"

offending_extra_words: shall be conducted off-site wherever possible and
reasons: All six preferred atomic elements are satisfied on the face of the redlined text: annual frequency cap, 30 days' written notice, business-hours limitation, independent confidentiality-bound auditor, Vendor-borne cost, and an express bar on direct system access.
The cost element is met because HDI bears fees unconditionally; the 5% underpayment shift-back is an exception in Vendor's favour whose absence benefits Customer, so it is not a gap to be cured.

Minimality fails only on the added "conducted off-site wherever possible" language: the playbook requires no direct system access, which the following words already achieve, so this phrase is duplicated/extra protection beyond the selected level.

Intent is preserved — the untouched cost sentence, records scope and business-hours limits remain effective, and replacing "HDI's General Manager (as hereinafter defined)" with "HDI" introduces no undefined term or dangling mechanic.
Rule classification: compliant at the preferred level; no further redline needed beyond trimming the surplus off-site phrase.
